recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and declared-version fixes
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check gets recorded_versions (default FALSE): with TRUE, the R
packages the scripts load are installed at the versions in renv.lock, a
sessionInfo() or session_info() record, or a groundhog or checkpoint date. The R
version is not changed. On 16 repositories this took about 2.7 times as long and
no failing script started working, so it is not the default. When scripts fail
and a repository records versions, the report, summary and checklist recommend a
run with the setting; on a shared server they say it is not available there.

After installing recorded versions, a load check replaces a recorded version that
keeps a package from loading, or crashes R, with the current one.

code_check reads sessionInfo() records pasted into scripts, and no longer counts a
README in a revdep folder as a record.

Fixes found by running real repositories:
- Docker runs no longer write a crash file of about 2.5 GB per R crash on Windows
- installs on R 3.6 work: closed MRAN addresses go to the Posit copy of that date,
  remotes is installed when the image lacks it, results keep working without
  data.frame's newer defaults
- packages that keep the current version install before recorded ones
- a package gone from CRAN that is in the image or main library counts as present
- batch runs pass layout on
- a package that does not load is reported with R's own reason

The live ResearchBox test in test-module-repo_check.R skips when ResearchBox asks
for a captcha.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Real reasons for files not fetched; KNB identifiers; reported results compared again
recent_commits.body:
Fixes found during a run over 1861 papers:

- reproducibility_check compared no output with the paper when given a list of
  one paper: match_reported_output() stopped on it and the module hid the error.
- The data manifest called every file in an archive "no download URL"; it now
  gives the real reason, such as the size limit or the archive's error. A file
  in an archive with no size is reported, not dropped.
- DataONE: file identifiers with slashes are kept whole; a file with no usable
  identifier is found by file name; the search works on KNB, which labels its
  reply text/json.
- Dataverse: restricted files are not requested and are reported as skipped; a
  guestbook requirement is named in the error.
- repo_check removes the punctuation that ends a sentence from an address, which
  made one repository into two.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.body:
A docker info that took more than 15 seconds was reported as Docker not
running, which stopped the paper. A late answer now gets two more tries, of
30 and 60 seconds. If all three are late, the message says Docker did not
answer. An error answer still reports at once that Docker is not running.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Reuse saved archive files (#561); make saved file names safe on every system (#557)
recent_commits.body:
Files inside an archive that were already saved are now found by their
size and reused, so they are not fetched or unpacked again on every run.

Names that are not valid on some operating system (a colon, * ? " < > |,
control characters, a final dot or space, reserved names) are now changed
in the same way on every system, wherever metacheck saves a file. A script
that cannot be written no longer stops reproducibility_check for the paper.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.body: Each table of a file with several has its columns under source_file = "file.xlsx [sheet]", and a new column sheet names the sheet; a file with one table keeps its own name. Sheets of notes and codebooks are documentation when the file has another table. FAIR_repo() names each variable's CSV by its sheet, writes a CSV per sheet of an .ods file, and writes dataset_description.json also when the first sheet's CSV went to documentation/.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
recent_commits.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
recent_commits.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: API keys work the same way for every repository, and visitors can use their own when the server's run out
recent_commits.body:
- R/api-keys.R: each key is read from an option first and an environment
  variable second, checked once per R session, and left out with a warning
  when the service refuses it. A refused key or a reached limit is recorded in
  a state folder all R sessions share (METACHECK_STATE_DIR), and
  api_key_status() gives the message for the visitor. api_keys_use() sets a
  visitor's own keys for one job. New github_pat() and openalex_key().
- GitHub, GitLab, OSF, Dataverse, Dryad, ResearchBox and OpenAlex use this;
  keys go only to their own host; a GitHub or GitLab limit now reports the
  repository as not listed instead of empty; ResearchBox's count of "unfound"
  answers moved to the state folder, where it is no longer lost after each job.
- osf_app(): a wrong typed token no longer clears OSF_PAT.
- The three apps: a folded box "Your own API keys (optional)" and a notice
  when a key of the server was refused or used up; the keys go to the
  visitor's own job only. The plumber API takes key_<service> fields.
- Tests: setup.R's resets now run when all tests have run (teardown_env());
  before, they ran at once, so tests wrote to the package source and the
  user's own state folder. test-app-repocheck.R puts metacheck.repo_cache.dir
  back after the app's job.

recent_commits.message: Keep the groups in order when reverse_map_total_n() starts from a back pair
recent_commits.body:
* reverse_map_total_n() took the first two rows of each case as the first
and the second group. A "back" pair holds the second group's values in
its first row, since the mapper swaps the groups for that direction, so
after filter(dir == "back") or a sort by direction the reconstructed x1
and x2 (and sd1 and sd2) changed places, and audit_total_n() reported
the hits under the swapped groups. The two rows of a back pair now
change places first.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add up near-whole counts as whole numbers and reject bad n in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* add_up_to() accepted a near-whole value like 100 * 0.29 as whole but
compared it exactly, so add_up_to(c(10, 19), total = 100 * 0.29) was
FALSE. The values are rounded before the comparison, as every other
whole-number argument is.

* disperse(), disperse2(), and disperse_total() check that n is numeric
and finite before any arithmetic. A string, a logical, a missing value
in disperse2(), or an infinity used to fail with a raw R error from the
arithmetic, or in disperse_total(TRUE) to return no rows at all.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the findings of the grim_grid() audit
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() has a threshold argument for data without a recorded
one, so a plot without data can show any up_from raster. A test checks
that a recorded or given threshold reaches the raster.

* DESCRIPTION requires dplyr >= 1.1.0, which .by needs, as in
grim_plot_rates() and the grim_grid() example.

* grim_grid() says when digits is missing and gives one message for any
value other than 1, 2, or 3, without the digits_x wording about scaling
x. Length checks on rounding and threshold come before roundwork's
message, which names symmetric.

* The docs say three decimal places take about 20 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Point to grim_grid() in the GRIM vignette and keep R 4.1 support
recent_commits.body:
* The vignette no longer says the up_from family has no raster, and shows
grim_grid() with the share of means ruled out per sample size.

* grim_grid() docs say which digits to use for percentages.

* purrr::pluck() keeps the pipe in grim_grid_inconsistent() without the
_$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return every cell of the grid from grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* grim_grid() now has a consistency column and a row for every cell, so
rates such as the share of means ruled out per n are one summarise()
away. The cells are marked by position from the cached inconsistent
ones, which takes about half a millisecond for 2 decimal places.

* The cache is unchanged. grim_plot_grid() reads it through the new
internal grim_grid_inconsistent() and does no extra work.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename grim_raster() to grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* The function returns data, the grid's inconsistent cells, so it is
named after the grid that grim_plot_grid() draws, like grim_values() and
grim_plot_values(). "Raster" is left to the plot's drawing.

* GRIM_RASTERS and generate_grim_raster() follow suit; R/sysdata.rda
was regenerated and holds identical data under the new name.

* Back to $rounding instead of the _$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.

recent_commits.message: Draw grim_plot_grid()'s raster through grim_raster()
recent_commits.body:

and "fractional parts" in the symmetric comment and docs.

recent_commits.message: Add grim_raster() for the GRIM-inconsistent grid
recent_commits.body:

rounding methods, the up_from family with its threshold, and 3 decimal
places are computed on demand. More than 3 is an error.

* generate_grim_raster() moves from data-raw/data-gen.R into the package,
so the cache and the on-demand path share one generator.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say "integers" in the values docs and name every changed column in NEWS
recent_commits.body:
* The values functions admit negative integers, as GRIM admits negative
  means, so their docs say "integers", as NEWS and the GRIM vignette do,
  rather than "whole numbers".
* NEWS says that the `digits_*` columns are integer, and that the
  `is_seq_*()` functions return `TRUE` for one or two values with `NA`,
  not only for a vector of `NA` only.
* `function_map()`'s `.reported` doc says that the whole-number rule
  applies to a key or helper column, since `items_averaged` is a helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:

* as_integer_if_lossless()'s description had a 120-character line.

recent_commits.message: Return every whole-number key and helper column as integer
recent_commits.body:
* `function_map()` made only `n` integer, so `items_averaged` and
`absolute` came back as doubles next to an integer `n`. Now every
`ARGS_WHOLE` column of the output goes through `as_integer_if_lossless()`.

* Reflow the `ARGS_WHOLE` comment, which a54c2eb left with a three-word
line in the middle.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make only decimal counts integer among the by-row arguments
recent_commits.body:
* `function_map()` ran every `.args_by_row` value through
`as_integer_if_lossless()`, so a custom by-row argument such as `tol =
1e-8`, within tolerance of 0, was tested and returned as 0L. Now only
arguments named in `ARGS_WHOLE` or starting with `digits_` are, as
`.args_by_row` documents. Every by-row argument of scrutiny's own
mappers is such a decimal count.

* The `.reported` docs name the whole-number columns that `ARGS_WHOLE`
covers since a54c2eb.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body: * 5caeb39 broke the chain after its last pipe only.

recent_commits.message: Compare a near-whole n to the limits as the whole number in disperse()
recent_commits.body:
* `disperse()` filtered the raw `n` against `n_min` and `n_max` but
showed the group sizes as integers, so `disperse(2 - 1e-9, dispersion =
0:2)` lost the pair (1, 3), and `disperse(10 + 1e-9, dispersion = 0:3,
n_max = 12)` the pair (8, 12). `disperse2()` rounds its two values
itself, since their mean is no longer near-whole. The total-n mappers
were not affected: `disperse_total()` already rounded.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test a near-whole count in is_percentage_of() as the whole number
recent_commits.body:
* `is_percentage_of_scalar()` accepted an `absolute` within tolerance of a
whole number, then compared it to the range of counts as is:
`is_percentage_of(100 * 0.29, 72.5, 40, digits_percentage = 1)` was
FALSE, where 29 is TRUE, and so was `is_percentage_of_map()`. A
near-whole `digits_percentage` was used as is by `is_percentage_of()`,
though not by its mapper, which rounds by-row arguments.

* Both names join `ARGS_WHOLE`, so `map_value_sets()` and
`function_map()` round them like `n`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round near-whole arguments in the exports that read them directly
recent_commits.body:
* 5caeb39 rounded `n`, `items_averaged`, and `digits_*` only where they
pass through `function_map()`, `map_value_sets()`, the `*_explain()`
functions, `disperse_total()`, and the total-n body. Other exports used
the raw values. `grim_total()` and `grim_exp_incon()` counted ties off a
common divisor that needs whole numbers: `grim_exp_incon(1.5, 100 *
0.56, 2, 1)` was 0.44 rather than 0.4, `digits_x = 2 - 1e-9` at `n =
40` gave 60 inconsistent values rather than 40, and `n = 1 - 1e-9` was
`NA` where `grim()` decides. The `exp_incon` column of `grim_map()` was
right all along.

* The `sd_binary_*()` functions returned `NA` for `n = 2 - 1e-9`, the
comb plots refused `n` at the minimum as "0.999999999", and the
`*_explain()` functions wrote a near-whole `digits_*` as "0.999999999
decimal places". All of them now call `round_whole()` too.

* The NEWS item moves to the bug fixes and names the functions covered.
`function_map()` documents that it rounds columns of these names in
custom mappers as well.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round near-whole totals before the comment on rejecting them
recent_commits.body:
* 5caeb39 put the call between the comment on `offenders` and the code
it describes.

recent_commits.message: Restore the NEWS item on calling mappers through lapply()
recent_commits.body:
* aeddf6f cut it as describing a change within the branch, but 0.6.1's
`absorb_key_args()` read the key arguments off `rlang::caller_call()`,
which through `lapply()` is `FUN(X[[i]], ...)`, so `lapply(dfs, grim_map,
x = "mean")` could not find the renamed column there either.

recent_commits.message: Test a near-whole n as the whole number it is shown as
recent_commits.body:
* `is_whole_number()` accepts a value within 1.5e-8 of a whole number,
such as `100 * 0.29`, but the arithmetic used it as is. 5288581 rounded
the `n` column of mapper output, yet only after the test, so `grim_map(x
= 1.5, n = 2 - 1e-9, rounding = "ceiling")` was FALSE next to `n = 2`,
where it is TRUE; GRIMMER and DEBIT compared the raw value to their
minimum `n` of 2 and left the verdict NA; `disperse_total()` and the
total-n mappers split `40 - 1e-9` as odd, into 19.5 and 20.5.

* `round_whole()` rounds the values the tolerance accepts and leaves the
rest, which the tests reject as before. It runs at the export boundaries,
on the `ARGS_WHOLE` arguments: `function_map()`'s tested columns, which
the output now takes its key and helper columns from, `map_value_sets()`,
the `*_explain()` functions, `disperse_total()`, and the totals of the
total-n body. The `*_scalar()` functions see whole numbers only.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the stable core of 1.0.0 in NEWS and the factory help pages
recent_commits.body:
* The release summary now says that the tests, the mapper tiers, and
audit() are stable, and that everything new in 1.0.0 and the developer
tools may change in a minor release. The bullet under "New features"
that said half of this is folded into it.

* The help pages of function_map(), function_map_seq(), and
function_map_total_n() carry the same note; until now only the pkgdown
reference index did.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round, not truncate, n and digits_* to integer
recent_commits.body:
* `as_integer_if_lossless()` admits values within tolerance of a whole number
but truncated them, so `n = 100 * 0.29` (28.999999999999996) was shown as 28
next to the verdict for 29. b8536d3 extended this to `digits_*`: a
`digits_x` just below 2 was shown as 1, and `grim_map_seq()` then failed.
* `function_map()` and `function_map_seq()` turn `digits_*` into integers
before testing or dispersing, so the column is the value used. Non-numeric
input passes through unchanged, for `fn()`'s own error.
* Two long lines in `R/utils.R` and `R/function-map.R` formatted with air.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check only single-value defaults for length in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 required every setting to be length 1, so a mapper made from a
`.fn` with a setting such as `bounds = NULL` or `scale = c(1, 7)` failed on
every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the length error for length-2 settings in two stale tests
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 checks every setting's length before its value, so
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` and `percent = c(TRUE, FALSE)` now fail with
"must be length 1, not 2". Two expectations still had the old wording.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the digits_* columns as integers in all mapper tiers
recent_commits.body:
* `n` was already integer when lossless, but `digits_x` and `digits_sd` were
double although they are always whole numbers. `function_map()` and
`function_map_seq()` now pass them through `as_integer_if_lossless()`; the
total-n tier inherits the basic mapper's columns.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut NEWS items that describe changes since 0.6.1 only within the branch
recent_commits.body:
* Each item was checked against scrutiny 0.6.1, installed from main. Dropped:
the integer `digits_*` columns, the `items = 2` partial match, the error for
two key arguments naming one column, the `grim_binomial()` and
`grim_plot_rates()` clause, GRIMMER running indefinitely, the integer
`diff_var`, `1e-300` having 315 decimal places, and mappers failing under
`lapply()`.
* Reworded items that 0.6.1 handled differently from the stated earlier
state: a seq mapper with nothing to disperse already warned, and a total-n
case without group pairs failed rather than vanishing.
* `grim_map(percent = TRUE)` now says that `x` stays a percentage, which is
the actual change from 0.6.1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require every setting to be length 1 in the mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers checked the settings with `check_lengths_congruent()`,
which allowed one of them to be longer than 1. An enum such as
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` then reached `rlang::arg_match()`,
whose error says it is 'not "se"', though "se" is valid; `percent =
c(TRUE, FALSE)` reached the test. The vectorized functions had their
own length-1 check with a better message.

* `check_setting_length()` is that check, shared by `map_value_sets()`,
`function_map()`, and the total-n factory, which reads an enum before
`fn()` does. In the mappers it runs after `check_rounding_args()`, which
keeps its own message for the rounding arguments.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` had no caller left and is deleted with its
tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
recent_commits.body:
* `check_values_size()` formatted the value set with `format()`'s
default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

and ties_* resolution live in one place.

and "fractional parts" in the symmetric comment and docs.

_new_commits.body:

rounding methods, the up_from family with its threshold, and 3 decimal
places are computed on demand. More than 3 is an error.

so the cache and the on-demand path share one generator.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Say "integers" in the values docs and name every changed column in NEWS
_new_commits.body:
* The values functions admit negative integers, as GRIM admits negative
  means, so their docs say "integers", as NEWS and the GRIM vignette do,
  rather than "whole numbers".
* NEWS says that the `digits_*` columns are integer, and that the
  `is_seq_*()` functions return `TRUE` for one or two values with `NA`,
  not only for a vector of `NA` only.

  applies to a key or helper column, since `items_averaged` is a helper.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Name every count in the near-whole NEWS item and rewrap a doc comment
_new_commits.body:

  none of the three counts it named.
* as_integer_if_lossless()'s description had a 120-character line.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Return every whole-number key and helper column as integer
_new_commits.body:
* `function_map()` made only `n` integer, so `items_averaged` and
`absolute` came back as doubles next to an integer `n`. Now every
`ARGS_WHOLE` column of the output goes through `as_integer_if_lossless()`.

* Reflow the `ARGS_WHOLE` comment, which a54c2eb left with a three-word
line in the middle.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Make only decimal counts integer among the by-row arguments
_new_commits.body:
* `function_map()` ran every `.args_by_row` value through
`as_integer_if_lossless()`, so a custom by-row argument such as `tol =
1e-8`, within tolerance of 0, was tested and returned as 0L. Now only
arguments named in `ARGS_WHOLE` or starting with `digits_` are, as
`.args_by_row` documents. Every by-row argument of scrutiny's own
mappers is such a decimal count.

* The `.reported` docs name the whole-number columns that `ARGS_WHOLE`
covers since a54c2eb.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Break the near-whole total-n expectation into parallel lines
_new_commits.body: * 5caeb39 broke the chain after its last pipe only.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Compare a near-whole n to the limits as the whole number in disperse()
_new_commits.body:
* `disperse()` filtered the raw `n` against `n_min` and `n_max` but
showed the group sizes as integers, so `disperse(2 - 1e-9, dispersion =
0:2)` lost the pair (1, 3), and `disperse(10 + 1e-9, dispersion = 0:3,
n_max = 12)` the pair (8, 12). `disperse2()` rounds its two values
itself, since their mean is no longer near-whole. The total-n mappers
were not affected: `disperse_total()` already rounded.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Test a near-whole count in is_percentage_of() as the whole number
_new_commits.body:
* `is_percentage_of_scalar()` accepted an `absolute` within tolerance of a
whole number, then compared it to the range of counts as is:
`is_percentage_of(100 * 0.29, 72.5, 40, digits_percentage = 1)` was
FALSE, where 29 is TRUE, and so was `is_percentage_of_map()`. A
near-whole `digits_percentage` was used as is by `is_percentage_of()`,
though not by its mapper, which rounds by-row arguments.

* Both names join `ARGS_WHOLE`, so `map_value_sets()` and
`function_map()` round them like `n`.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

_new_commits.message: Round near-whole arguments in the exports that read them directly
_new_commits.body:
* 5caeb39 rounded `n`, `items_averaged`, and `digits_*` only where they
pass through `function_map()`, `map_value_sets()`, the `*_explain()`
functions, `disperse_total()`, and the total-n body. Other exports used
the raw values. `grim_total()` and `grim_exp_incon()` counted ties off a
common divisor that needs whole numbers: `grim_exp_incon(1.5, 100 *
0.56, 2, 1)` was 0.44 rather than 0.4, `digits_x = 2 - 1e-9` at `n =
40` gave 60 inconsistent values rather than 40, and `n = 1 - 1e-9` was
`NA` where `grim()` decides. The `exp_incon` column of `grim_map()` was
right all along.

* The `sd_binary_*()` functions returned `NA` for `n = 2 - 1e-9`, the
comb plots refused `n` at the minimum as "0.999999999", and the
`*_explain()` functions wrote a near-whole `digits_*` as "0.999999999
decimal places". All of them now call `round_whole()` too.

* The NEWS item moves to the bug fixes and names the functions covered.
`function_map()` documents that it rounds columns of these names in
custom mappers as well.
_new_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.

(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: run every script that parses, and do not predict built names as missing (#568)
highlights.body:
Scripts with a predicted missing file are no longer skipped. The prediction was
partly wrong and the skip hid how far a script gets. Names that cannot be checked
before the code runs (paste() and sprintf() calls, placeholders, pieces of names)
are no longer predicted as missing. After a run, the report lists only inputs in
the deposit that are not usable as named. Tests added but not yet run.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Merge pull request #567 from scienceverse/recorded_versions
highlights.body: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and R 3.6 fixes
highlights.author: Daniel Lakens

highlights.message: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and declared-version fixes
highlights.body:
reproducibility_check gets recorded_versions (default FALSE): with TRUE, the R
packages the scripts load are installed at the versions in renv.lock, a
sessionInfo() or session_info() record, or a groundhog or checkpoint date. The R
version is not changed. On 16 repositories this took about 2.7 times as long and
no failing script started working, so it is not the default. When scripts fail
and a repository records versions, the report, summary and checklist recommend a
run with the setting; on a shared server they say it is not available there.

After installing recorded versions, a load check replaces a recorded version that
keeps a package from loading, or crashes R, with the current one.

code_check reads sessionInfo() records pasted into scripts, and no longer counts a
README in a revdep folder as a record.

Fixes found by running real repositories:
- Docker runs no longer write a crash file of about 2.5 GB per R crash on Windows
- installs on R 3.6 work: closed MRAN addresses go to the Posit copy of that date,
  remotes is installed when the image lacks it, results keep working without
  data.frame's newer defaults
- packages that keep the current version install before recorded ones
- a package gone from CRAN that is in the image or main library counts as present
- batch runs pass layout on
- a package that does not load is reported with R's own reason

The live ResearchBox test in test-module-repo_check.R skips when ResearchBox asks
for a captcha.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Bump Authlib 1.7.2 -> 1.9.1 for new security advisories
highlights.body:
CI's dependency audit started failing on eight advisories published
against Authlib 1.7.2 (PYSEC-2026-4354..4360, CVE-2026-96760,
CVE-2026-116672); 1.9.1 fixes all of them. Only authlib changes in the
hash-locked requirements.lock.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
highlights.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
highlights.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: One canonical text per document
highlights.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
highlights.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
highlights.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
highlights.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
highlights.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
highlights.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
highlights.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
highlights.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
highlights.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
highlights.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
highlights.author: Jamie Cummins

highlights.message: Check the types in grim_values(), name a bad constant element, rebuild README
highlights.body:
* grim_values() and grim_closest() run the same input checks as grim():
a string n or items_averaged is an error, not an undecidable value set
with a row of NA, and a percent that is not TRUE or FALSE is an error
in them and in grim_plot_values(), through a shared check_percent().

* A constant list element of the wrong length is reported under the
user's name for it, such as `constant$z`, instead of the internal
variable, and without the purrr "In index" contexts, which made an
error about the argument look like one about a row.

highlights.message: Keep the groups in order when reverse_map_total_n() starts from a back pair
highlights.body:
* reverse_map_total_n() took the first two rows of each case as the first
and the second group. A "back" pair holds the second group's values in
its first row, since the mapper swaps the groups for that direction, so
after filter(dir == "back") or a sort by direction the reconstructed x1
and x2 (and sd1 and sd2) changed places, and audit_total_n() reported
the hits under the swapped groups. The two rows of a back pair now
change places first.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Add up near-whole counts as whole numbers and reject bad n in disperse*()
highlights.body:
* add_up_to() accepted a near-whole value like 100 * 0.29 as whole but
compared it exactly, so add_up_to(c(10, 19), total = 100 * 0.29) was
FALSE. The values are rounded before the comparison, as every other
whole-number argument is.

* disperse(), disperse2(), and disperse_total() check that n is numeric
and finite before any arithmetic. A string, a logical, a missing value
in disperse2(), or an infinity used to fail with a raw R error from the
arithmetic, or in disperse_total(TRUE) to return no rows at all.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix the findings of the grim_grid() audit
highlights.body:
* grim_plot_grid() has a threshold argument for data without a recorded
one, so a plot without data can show any up_from raster. A test checks
that a recorded or given threshold reaches the raster.

* DESCRIPTION requires dplyr >= 1.1.0, which .by needs, as in
grim_plot_rates() and the grim_grid() example.

* grim_grid() says when digits is missing and gives one message for any
value other than 1, 2, or 3, without the digits_x wording about scaling
x. Length checks on rounding and threshold come before roundwork's
message, which names symmetric.

* The docs say three decimal places take about 20 seconds.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Point to grim_grid() in the GRIM vignette and keep R 4.1 support
highlights.body:
* The vignette no longer says the up_from family has no raster, and shows
grim_grid() with the share of means ruled out per sample size.

* grim_grid() docs say which digits to use for percentages.

* purrr::pluck() keeps the pipe in grim_grid_inconsistent() without the
_$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Return every cell of the grid from grim_grid()
highlights.body:
* grim_grid() now has a consistency column and a row for every cell, so
rates such as the share of means ruled out per n are one summarise()
away. The cells are marked by position from the cached inconsistent
ones, which takes about half a millisecond for 2 decimal places.

* The cache is unchanged. grim_plot_grid() reads it through the new
internal grim_grid_inconsistent() and does no extra work.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Rename grim_raster() to grim_grid()
highlights.body:
* The function returns data, the grid's inconsistent cells, so it is
named after the grid that grim_plot_grid() draws, like grim_values() and
grim_plot_values(). "Raster" is left to the plot's drawing.

* GRIM_RASTERS and generate_grim_raster() follow suit; R/sysdata.rda
was regenerated and holds identical data under the new name.

* Back to $rounding instead of the _$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.

highlights.message: Draw grim_plot_grid()'s raster through grim_raster()
highlights.body:
* The plot passes the recorded rounding and threshold to grim_raster(),
so the up_from family gets a raster instead of an error, and the lookup
and ties_* resolution live in one place.

* Includes the user's edits to grim_raster(): blank lines between steps
and "fractional parts" in the symmetric comment and docs.

highlights.message: Add grim_raster() for the GRIM-inconsistent grid
highlights.body:

rounding methods, the up_from family with its threshold, and 3 decimal
places are computed on demand. More than 3 is an error.

so the cache and the on-demand path share one generator.

highlights.body:
* The values functions admit negative integers, as GRIM admits negative
  means, so their docs say "integers", as NEWS and the GRIM vignette do,

`absolute` came back as doubles next to an integer `n`. Now every

highlights.body:

`as_integer_if_lossless()`, so a custom by-row argument such as `tol =
1e-8`, within tolerance of 0, was tested and returned as 0L. Now only
arguments named in `ARGS_WHOLE` or starting with `digits_` are, as
`.args_by_row` documents. Every by-row argument of scrutiny's own
mappers is such a decimal count.

highlights.message: Compare a near-whole n to the limits as the whole number in disperse()
highlights.body:
* `disperse()` filtered the raw `n` against `n_min` and `n_max` but
showed the group sizes as integers, so `disperse(2 - 1e-9, dispersion =
0:2)` lost the pair (1, 3), and `disperse(10 + 1e-9, dispersion = 0:3,
n_max = 12)` the pair (8, 12). `disperse2()` rounds its two values
itself, since their mean is no longer near-whole. The total-n mappers
were not affected: `disperse_total()` already rounded.

highlights.message: Test a near-whole count in is_percentage_of() as the whole number
highlights.body:
* `is_percentage_of_scalar()` accepted an `absolute` within tolerance of a
whole number, then compared it to the range of counts as is:
`is_percentage_of(100 * 0.29, 72.5, 40, digits_percentage = 1)` was
FALSE, where 29 is TRUE, and so was `is_percentage_of_map()`. A
near-whole `digits_percentage` was used as is by `is_percentage_of()`,
though not by its mapper, which rounds by-row arguments.

* Both names join `ARGS_WHOLE`, so `map_value_sets()` and
`function_map()` round them like `n`.

highlights.message: Round near-whole arguments in the exports that read them directly
highlights.body:
* 5caeb39 rounded `n`, `items_averaged`, and `digits_*` only where they
pass through `function_map()`, `map_value_sets()`, the `*_explain()`
functions, `disperse_total()`, and the total-n body. Other exports used
the raw values. `grim_total()` and `grim_exp_incon()` counted ties off a
common divisor that needs whole numbers: `grim_exp_incon(1.5, 100 *
0.56, 2, 1)` was 0.44 rather than 0.4, `digits_x = 2 - 1e-9` at `n =
40` gave 60 inconsistent values rather than 40, and `n = 1 - 1e-9` was
`NA` where `grim()` decides. The `exp_incon` column of `grim_map()` was
right all along.

* The `sd_binary_*()` functions returned `NA` for `n = 2 - 1e-9`, the
comb plots refused `n` at the minimum as "0.999999999", and the
`*_explain()` functions wrote a near-whole `digits_*` as "0.999999999
decimal places". All of them now call `round_whole()` too.

* The NEWS item moves to the bug fixes and names the functions covered.
`function_map()` documents that it rounds columns of these names in
custom mappers as well.

such as `100 * 0.29`, but the arithmetic used it as is. 5288581 rounded
the `n` column of mapper output, yet only after the test, so `grim_map(x

highlights.message: fix: caption-only table extent, W0p page-bound superscripts, grid-copy suppression, styled headings, stacked header labels, canary fixes
highlights.body:
Tables - A caption-only region takes its width and depth from its own rules; a whitespace region is extended to the table's closing rule; worded rows in a rule-bounded region are not trimmed as prose. - Side-by-side text lines in one Camelot cell keep page order and a space; a row label that runs on past the stub column returns to it. Both run only after the table gates (convert, then re-convert with telemetry discarded, kept only with an unchanged shape). - Stacked column-label lines fold into one header row (joined with
, as the super-header fold); not onto a data row, an unclosed parenthesis or a lost-glyph line. A single long line over the stub (panel label, stray caption line) is no longer folded into the stub label. - A fourth header row only under stacked label lines. Text and render - W0p superscript marking bound to its page and token; raised-sign exponents. - S8m: a significance mark printed on its own line rejoins its p-value legend. - Lines the render copies from a structured table are suppressed in the body; title rescue folds caret markers; RULE 0g / caption tail lines. - Lines set in the paper's heading face become headings (two- and three-line headings joined, run-in headings refused); a smaller size of a face whose larger size is a ### heading is emitted ####. Every change carries a regression test watched failing first; two-arm render diffs over a 128-paper sample were read against page images by a second model.

running, which stopped the paper. A late answer now gets two more tries, of

highlights.body:
Files inside an archive that were already saved are now found by their
size and reused, so they are not fetched or unpacked again on every run.

Names that are not valid on some operating system (a colon, * ? " < > |,
control characters, a final dot or space, reserved names) are now changed
in the same way on every system, wherever metacheck saves a file. A script
that cannot be written no longer stops reproducibility_check for the paper.
